name: Call one cached Bright Data scraper as a sub-workflow from any n8n workflow

parameters.content:
## One scraper your other workflows call, with a cache in front of it

By the fifth workflow that fetches a page you have written the same Bright Data call, the same error check and the same fallback five times. This is that code, once, as a **sub-workflow** other workflows call with a URL.

### How it works

It starts on an **Execute Workflow Trigger** - no schedule, no webhook. A caller passes `url`, optionally a `format` (`markdown`, `html` or `json`) and a `max_age_minutes`.

First it looks in the cache. A Data Table keeps every result with a timestamp, so asking for the same URL inside your freshness window returns instantly and **spends nothing**. Five workflows checking the same page each morning become one request.

On a miss it fetches through Bright Data, then checks the payload properly: Bright Data returns validation errors and blocks with **HTTP 200 and an error body**, and an empty body means the domain never resolved. If the result is empty or suspiciously thin it retries once with `render: true`, running the page in a real browser - which is what rescues single-page apps.

It always returns the same fields, including `ok`, `from_cache` and `error`, so the caller can branch on the result instead of guessing.

### Setup

1. A Bright Data Header Auth credential and a Web Unlocker zone.

2. A Data Table called `scrape_cache` with columns `url`, `content`, `status` and `fetched_at`. It will not add missing ones.

3. In another workflow, add **Execute Sub-workflow**, pick this one, pass a `url`.

## 1. Another workflow calls in
No schedule and no webhook. A caller passes a url, and optionally a format and how stale an answer it will accept.

## 2. Have we already got this?
The Data Table keeps every result with a timestamp. Inside the freshness window this returns instantly and spends nothing at all.

## 3. Fetch it, then actually check it
Bright Data answers validation errors and blocks with HTTP 200 and an error body. This is the check every caller would otherwise have to write.

## 4. Empty or thin? Try a browser
A shell of a document means the content is built in JavaScript. One retry with render on, never as the default, because rendering is slow.

## 5. One shape, whichever path got here
ok, from_cache and error are always present, so the caller branches on the result instead of guessing what came back.

## 6. Keep it for next time
Last, and off the return path. A Data Table problem must never stop the caller getting the content it already has.

## The cache is the point, so set the age deliberately

`max_age_minutes` decides whether this saves you money or hands you stale data. A competitor's pricing page changes monthly and can sit at `1440`; a stock level or a status page changes by the minute and should be `0`, which skips the cache entirely.

Pass it per call, not globally. The same scraper serving a daily digest and a live check wants two different answers, and the caller is the only one that knows which is which.

The cache key is the exact URL including its query string, so `?utm_source=` on the end makes a different entry. Strip tracking parameters before calling if you want them to share a row.
